goals: mechanistic: characterize vertical water balance and sub-surface drainage flux (recharge to lateral system) at contrasting hillslope positions
requested-but-infeasible: compute hillslope-to-stream travel times, lateral flow convergence along flowpaths, and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange
key_processes: LATERAL saturated/unsaturated flow along topographic gradient (not representable)
flow convergence and advective travel time (not representable)
groundwater exchange between neighboring columns (not representable)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column can produce per-position vertical water balance and drainage flux, which is the boundary forcing a lateral model would need — but it cannot itself resolve lateral transport, convergence, or travel time.
model_choice.coupling_note: Travel time, convergence, and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange require an explicit lateral flow / routing coupler (ELM QDRAI/recharge -> a hillslope or subsurface lateral model such as PFLOTRAN with a topographic mesh). This coupler is NOT implemented; see requires_capabilities.

answerable: vertical water partitioning and drainage/recharge flux (QDRAI) at individual hillslope positions
how soil texture and NLDAS forcing modulate the vertical recharge signal that would feed a lateral model

not_answerable.why: SINGLE-COLUMN, NO LATERAL TRANSPORT — columns are independent 1-D points with no routing or advection, so travel time along a flowpath cannot be computed
not_answerable.needs: lateral flow / flowpath routing coupler with residence-time tracking

not_answerable.aspect: lateral flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
not_answerable.why: no column-to-column exchange and no terrain-following lateral solver; convergence is inherently multi-cell lateral physics ELM omits
not_answerable.needs: topographically-connected lateral subsurface model (e.g. ELM->PFLOTRAN coupling on a hillslope mesh)

not_answerable.aspect: groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
not_answerable.why: no lateral/regional groundwater flow between columns; each column has an independent 1-D aquifer

classes: SSURGO native per position (thinner/coarser upslope, deeper/finer in valley)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: Four positions span the hillslope catena that a lateral model would connect; this yields the per-position vertical recharge/drainage flux precursors. More columns cannot buy lateral information the stack cannot compute, so N is kept minimal.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Points arranged down a single well-defined hillslope flowpath (ridge -> valley) so the outputs are directly usable as ordered boundary fluxes for a future lateral coupler; oversample the footslope/riparian bottom where storage and drainage sensitivity are highest.
sampling_strategy.replication: none — single transect; replication across multiple hillslopes is only worthwhile once a lateral coupler exists to consume it

sampling_plan.reason: recharge-dominated position; provides upslope drainage flux that would source a lateral flowpath
transit position along the catena; characterizes mid-flowpath vertical drainage
convergence/accumulation zone; highest sensitivity of drainage to initialized storage
discharge position near stream; drainage flux here is the terminal boundary a routing model needs

validation_design.target_variable: sub-surface drainage flux (QDRAI) / vertical water balance
validation_design.comparison: analog — physical-expectation check only (recharge decreasing downslope, storage/drainage increasing toward valley)
validation_design.metric: qualitative consistency with catena expectation; flux magnitudes vs literature

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up years

requires_capabilities.capability: lateral flow / flowpath routing coupler with residence-time tracking
requires_capabilities.why: the user asks for hillslope-to-stream travel times, which are advective transport quantities

requires_capabilities.capability: topographically-connected lateral subsurface model (ELM->PFLOTRAN on a hillslope mesh)
requires_capabilities.why: flow convergence along flowpaths is multi-cell lateral physics
groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions is not representable in independent 1-D columns
to pass per-position recharge/drainage fluxes as transient BCs into a lateral solver
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire coupled workflow that would answer the question

requires_capabilities.why: to define the ridge-to-valley transect and downstream connectivity
requires_capabilities.blocks: defensible placement of the catena transect

requires_capabilities.why: valley/footslope drainage depends on initialized water table and aquifer storage

assumptions: Naches lies within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 12 km forcing applies with orographic precip variation across the transect.
SSURGO soil is available per column; valley soils assumed deeper/finer than ridge.
A single representative hillslope adequately illustrates the vertical-flux precursors; the framework cannot connect the four positions laterally.
open_questions: Is a lateral-flow/routing coupler on the development roadmap? Without it the core question cannot be answered.
Are any WTD, streamflow, or soil-moisture observations obtainable for the Naches to constrain the vertical fluxes?
Which specific hillslope/flowpath should the transect follow — is there a target sub-catchment of interest?
